nodes.name: CWO Nanocuboids Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: In a typical synthesis of CWO nanocuboids, 2 mmol of Na₂WO₄·2H₂O and 4 mmol of CTAB were taken in a 100 mL beaker. 42 mL milli-Q water was added to it and stirred vigorously until a clear solution was formed (solution A). Meanwhile, in a 50 mL beaker, 3 mmol of Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O were taken and to it 20 mL of milli-Q water was poured. The solution was then stirred to acquire a bright red coloured Co (II)-aqueous solution (B). Next, solution B was added to the solution A and the mixture stirred vigorously to get a homogeneous solution. The resultant violet coloured solution mixture was then transferred to a 100 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and kept at 180°C for 12 h. After 12 h, the autoclave was cooled naturally down to room temperature. A blue-coloured product was collected and washed several times using milli-Q water and acetone.

nodes.name: CWO-del-48 Delamination (48h KOH)
nodes.procedure: The delaminated (CWO-del) compounds were obtained by immersing CoWO4 (CWO) in 0.1 M aqueous KOH solution under magnetic stirring for 48 h. Under continuous stirring, the blue coloured CWO turned to a brown to a black coloured product. The post-processed product was then washed and centrifuged for five times with milli-Q water and acetone. Finally, the obtained CWO-del-48 powder was obtained after centrifugation and annealing at 90°C overnight.

nodes.name: CWO-del-48 Ink on GCE
nodes.procedure: To prepare the catalyst ink, 10 mg of CWO-del-48 catalyst and 2.5 mg Vulcan carbon powder were dispersed in a mixture solution of 750 μL of milli-Q water, 150 μL of ethanol, 80 μL of iso-propanol and 20 μL of Nafion solution (5 wt.% in lower aliphatic alcohol). After sonication for 1 h., the catalyst-ink was drop-casted on pre-polished glassy carbon electrode (GCE, geometric surface area: 0.07 cm²). The catalyst loading on GCE: ~0.5 mg·cm⁻².

nodes.characterization_summary: CWO shows uniform cube-like nanocuboid morphology. CWO-del transforms from cuboids to flake-like morphology after 24-48h KOH treatment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The clockwise SEM study revealed the change in morphology of the nanocrystals... After 24 h KOH treatment, the cuboid CWO transformed into flake-like morphology.

nodes.characterization_summary: CWO nanocuboids show uniform cube-like morphology with (111) lattice spacing of 2.91 Å. CWO-del-48 shows flake-like shape with (010) crystal plane and stacking fault defects from WO4^2- leaching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM shows the regular crystal planes of the CWO nanocube. The lattice spacing of 2.91 Å, matches with the (111) crystal plane... The high-resolution TEM image displays the (010) crystal plane... with stacking fault defects.

nodes.characterization_summary: CWO shows cube-like structure with resolved (110), (100), (111), (011) planes along [011] zone axis. CWO-del-48 shows flake-like morphology with (011), (111), (102) planes along [211] zone axis and surface vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High angle annular dark field STEM (HAADF-STEM) image shows a cube-like structure of CWO... the corresponding fast Fourier transformed (FFT) image displays (110), (100), (111) and (011) crystal planes.

nodes.characterization_summary: CWO-del-48 shows missing O-atoms and W-vacancies from WO4^2- leaching. Atomic resolution reveals irregular surface termination with vacancies and monoatomic steps.
nodes.evidence_snippet: iDPC-STEM image shows the missing O-atoms (white circled), and HAADF-STEM micrographs of CWO–del–48 exhibits W-vacancies... The surface presents irregular termination with vacancies and monoatomic steps.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform elemental distribution of Co, W, O in both CWO and CWO-del-48 nanocuboids and flakes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The STEM-EDS mapping indicate the uniform elemental distribution of Co, W and O across the CWO nanocuboids... demonstrate the uniform elemental distribution of Co, W and O across the CWO-del-48 nanocrystals.

nodes.characterization_summary: CWO-del-48 shows decreased W content compared to CWO, confirming WO4^2- leaching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To assess the leaching of W after delamination, we performed EELS spectra of both CWO and CWO–del–48. As compared with the CWO, a decrease on the W content in CWO–del–48 can be confirmed.

nodes.characterization_summary: CWO-del-48 shows negligible decrease in Co (7.95→5.03 at.%) and W (13.52→10.24 at.%) after PEMWE operation, demonstrating stability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS analysis performed on CWO-del-48 before and after electrolysis in the PEMWE configuration reveals a negligible decrease in Co and W at.%

nodes.characterization_summary: CWO optical bandgap 2.8 eV reduces to 2.47 eV (CWO-del-24) and 2.25 eV (CWO-del-48) after KOH delamination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The optical bandgap of as-synthesized CWO is 2.8 eV. After 24 and 48 h of 0.1 M KOH treatment, the bandgap of CWO-del-24 and CWO-del-48 is reduced to 2.47 eV and 2.25 eV

nodes.characterization_summary: Dunk test: CWO-del-48 leaches 2.85, 4.82, 4.58 ppm Co after 10, 25, 50h in 0.5M H2SO4 (total 0.142 wt.% loss); CWO: 16.35-48.57 ppm; Co3O4: 25.65-32.64 ppm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. S1. Chemical stability test by dunk experiment... CWO–del–48 exhibited significantly lower leached Co ions concentration of 2.85, 4.82 and 4.58 ppm after 10, 25 and 50 h... The total Co ions leaching from 20 mg of CWO–del–48 after 50 h... is ∼0.122 mg (0.142 wt.%)

nodes.characterization_summary: ICo-O/IW-O ratio increases from 0.17 (CWO) to 1.20 (CWO-del-48) after 48h, saturating after kinetic limitation of W-leaching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The intensity ratio (ICo-O/IW-O) of Co–O ∼690 cm-1 to W–O (⁓886 cm-1)... increases rapidly until 24 h, and starts saturating after 48 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES of CWO-del-48 shows right shift in absorption edge at 50% height compared to CWO, suggesting higher Co oxidation state after delamination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The right shift in absorption edge at 50% height in XANES... suggest potentially higher oxidation state of Co in CWO–del–48 than CWO

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge EXAFS shows shorter Co-O bond distance and new features after 2 Å in CWO-del-48. W L3-edge shows slight changes due to elemental leaching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transformed EXAFS (FT-EXAFS)... indicates that Co–O bond distance becomes shorter after delamination. Additionally, the new features after 2 Å radial distance in CWO-del-48
